content:
emily: FYI — acme-inc reported a bunch of 429s + slow responses after their midnight batch job (~00:12 UTC). They call it 'perceived throttling' even though monthly quota looks fine. I grabbed two sample request ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Their job does continuous batching of many short prompts (high cardinality prefixes). Can we triage? /cc @maya

maya: Thanks Emily. Quick q's: hosted or dedicated? do we have the API key or tenant id? sample payload would help. I'll ping infra if it looks like platform limits.

emily: Hosted (standard plan). Tenant id: tenant_acme. Sample payload (sanitized):
```json
{"prompt":"tell me a 1-line summary","max_tokens":16}
```
Headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME123
Their pattern: 60k requests over a 5 minute window, many very short prompts, repeated prefixes but lots of slightly different user/session ids.

billing-bot: quota-check: tenant_acme — monthly usage 94%, burst_pool_remaining: 4200 units, burst_window_sec: 10

jason: Looking at runtime metrics around 00:11-00:14 UTC: we see queue length growth and sudden increase in average batch_size from ~16 -> ~64. Batch wait latency jumped and per-tenant concurrency cap hit; that's when we returned most 429s. Also noticed kvcache hit rate dropped to ~12% during the spike.

anil: That matches prefix-churn + continuous batching interactions. If the batcher groups many different prefixes, KV cache locality collapses and we end up doing lots of extra work + backpressure. This often reads to customers as "throttling" because requests wait in queue or get 429s when concurrency cap is reached.

maya: Can you sketch immediate mitigations? We need steps we can run now and recommend to the customer for longer-term fixes.

anil: Immediate (fast) options:
- temporarily raise tenant_acme max_concurrency for 10-30m to drain backlog
- enable short-term KVCACHE prewarm for their top prefixes
- ask customer to add jitter to their batch windows so jobs don't align with our batching snapshot boundaries

Example override to push now:
```yaml
tenant_overrides:
  tenant_acme:
    max_concurrency: 120   # increase from default 40
    prewarm_prefixes: ["user:acme", "session:acme"]
    batch_window_ms_override: 50
```

emily: Customer provided a small repro script we can replay once limits are adjusted — they can also gate the job to use fewer concurrent workers for now. Suggest we do a quick repro at low rate before bumping.

jason: I'll open escalation ticket INF-2023-556. Plan: bump concurrency to 120 for 15min at 00:18 UTC, run a controlled replay, monitor 429 rate + kvcache hitrate. @anil can you run a kvcache prewarm on the specified prefixes?

anil: On it. Also adding a note: long-term we should add a per-tenant sticky-routing option so requests with the same cache prefix route to the same worker pool — reduces prefix starvation under continuous batching. Filing RFC after this triage.

maya: Quick customer-facing guidance to send: 1) add 100-200ms jitter to batch start times, 2) reduce per-job concurrency by ~30% during high-volume windows, 3) consider grouping requests by explicit prefix (e.g., include stable "user:acme" key) so the KV cache can be effective.

deploy-bot: deploy-ops: no infra deploys during 00:10-00:20 UTC window.

jason: Update — bumped tenant_acme to 120 at 00:18 UTC. Observed 429 rate drop from 8.6% -> 0.9% within 2 minutes, kvcache hitrate recovered to ~48%. Leaving override for 30m and will revert unless customer requests extension.

emily: Customer confirmed improved latency and fewer 429s. They will implement jitter and prefix grouping in next deployment. Closing loop once they ship. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
